market_definition: Observed annual value of insect-derived meal sold as animal-feed input within each country; product/year/currency/coverage must be explicit. This packet does not substitute production, capacity, project output or all-feed market totals.

definitions.national_insect_meal_market: Observed annual domestic sales value of insect-derived meal sold as an animal-feed ingredient, with species/product definition and country coverage; do not include live insects, oil, frass, generic compound feed or forecast revenue unless separately measured and labelled.
definitions.cost_outcomes: Diet ingredient price, formulated-feed cost per kg, feed intake, FCR (feed per bodyweight gain), feed cost per kg gain, total farm production cost and retail chicken price are different outcomes.
definitions.mechanism: As an accounting identity for compatible units, feed cost per kg liveweight gain equals formulated-feed cost per kg multiplied by FCR. Other farm costs, yield, mortality, processing, transport, regulation and margins affect chicken cost. This identity supplies no parameter or observed causal effect.
definitions.eligibility: Feed is an input to poultry production and is excluded from human-protein totals; no demand elasticity, adoption weight or halal verdict follows from these economic records.

ethnography.paragraph: Field studies in Arunachal Pradesh document insect collection and eating among particular communities: Nyishi and Galo respondents in East Kameng and West Siang in a study published in 2011, and six groups in Tirap and Changlang in a study published in 2013. Each study interviewed 20 informants per group. The former explicitly describes its evidence as qualitative; both concern situated knowledge and uses rather than representative consumption prevalence. The studies share an author and research programme. These accounts do not describe all South Asia, establish medicinal efficacy, or provide human-protein demand totals; publication years are not established fieldwork dates.

scope_rules: Input species/purity, substrate, insect state, processing, feeding mixture and eventual poultry status are separate.
Human-insect consumption rules do not automatically establish feed rules.
Named rulings are attributed, not school consensus or national product certification.
Feed never enters human alternative-protein demand totals.
